artifacts.title: Tail Certificates and Achievement-Set Geometry for Erdős Problems 249 and 257
artifacts.claim_scope: Gateway exposition for Erdős Problems 249 and 257. For #249 it records the exact dyadic-section rank 2^e+1 for e >= 1, infinite-dimensionality, the explicit finite Farey denominator exclusion, and diagonal certificates through t = 82, but no instance at t = 83 or unbounded family. For #257 it records checked restricted-support geometry and the remaining half-value and 1/21 branches. Both problems remain open, and the shared Lambert-series change of variables transfers no irrationality theorem.

artifacts.title: The Binary Totient Series
artifacts.claim_scope: Claim-bounded reasoning record for Erdős Problem 249. It distinguishes checked premises and finite certificates from open obligations: the level-e dyadic-section rank is 2^e+1 only for e >= 1; the full span is infinite-dimensional; the finite Farey computation excludes denominators up to the stated bound; and diagonal certificates exist through t = 82, with neither t = 83 nor an unbounded family supplied. Irrationality remains open.

artifacts.title: Reciprocal Mersenne Subseries
artifacts.claim_scope: Claim-bounded reasoning record for Erdős Problem 257. It gives complete ordinary arguments and records Lean proofs of the finite-prime weighted criterion, its hereditary base-two-host/all-base consequence, the strengthened positive-cover criterion, the common-scale mixed weighted/cover criterion, and the reciprocal-summable-support corollary without pairwise coprimality. Each theorem retains its stated infinitude, positivity, weighted-mass, cover-majorant, scaled-cost, host-containment, and common-witness hypotheses as applicable. The named separating examples and their divergent-reciprocal calculations are ordinary mathematics and are not themselves replayed in Lean. The record separately retains checked finite-support and restricted achievement-set structure: no finite rank-at-least-two support represents 1/21, while the eventual affine-supercapacity regime survives. The universal, half-value, and 1/21 membership questions remain open.

artifacts.title: Integral Relations among Totient Sections
artifacts.claim_scope: Standalone exposition of Erdős Problem 249, ordered unconditional results first: the exact level-e dyadic totient section rank 2^e+1 for e >= 1 (Lean) and the resulting infinite-dimensionality, which for integer-valued sequence modules is equivalent to Coons's non-k-regularity and is not an independent contribution; the all-base exact-rank upgrade uses Martin's external independence hypothesis. A separate ordinary argument treats bounded-residue series A_m. The explicit finite-Farey denominator exclusion and Lean diagonal certificates through t = 82 are finite; neither t = 83 nor an unbounded family is supplied. Irrationality remains open.

artifacts.title: Weighted and Covered Supports for Mersenne Subseries
artifacts.claim_scope: Standalone exposition of Erdős Problem 257. Lean proves the finite-prime weighted support criterion, its hereditary base-two-host/all-base consequence, the strengthened positive-cover criterion under its cover-majorant and summable scaled-cost hypotheses, and the mixed weighted/cover criterion using a common observation scale. Lean also proves that summable reciprocal-support mass suffices without pairwise coprimality. The named examples separating these criteria, including the displayed divergent-reciprocal host, use ordinary set and summability calculations and are not separately replayed as Lean theorems. These sufficient criteria retain their stated support hypotheses and do not cover arbitrary infinite supports. The universal, half-value, and 1/21 membership questions remain open; cited classical results and attribution remain distinct from local proof provenance.

artifacts.title: Integer Linear Forms for a\\Factorial Reciprocal Series
artifacts.claim_scope: Exposition of the ErdosProblems.Erdos68 modules. The Comparator isolation pin for the carry equivalences is FactorialGapPlateauCore; FactorialZeroPlateau is the default-root duplicate of that family, not the isolation source. Lean checks the exact factorial-successor and eventual-unit-carry frontiers, integral-channel and prime-translator identities, weighted projection consumers, and the Cramer residual identity. The paper also proves an all-index factorial-channel congruence and gives a shorter five-term depth-four moment witness; these new finite results are mathematical arguments, not Lean declarations. An independently regenerated exact GMP certificate supplies one non-unit carry at m = 300000, and a Lean theorem consumes that finite fact to exclude every smaller positive rational denominator; a separate continued-fraction bound gives q ≥ 2^39990. The two finite exclusions are incomparable. No theorem supplies cofinally many non-unit carries; Erdős Problem 68 remains open.

artifacts.title: Cubic-Rate Irrationality and Reciprocal-Tail Rigidity
artifacts.claim_scope: The note leads with cubic-rate irrationality for one-based strictly increasing positive integer sequences under a_n²/a_(n+1)=1+3/n+o(n^-3). Lean checks the zero-indexed positive StrictMono theorem; the finite-prefix transfer to the printed one-based form is an ordinary argument. The ordinary proof uses classical Chebotarev; the Lean square-specialisation proof instead uses Mathlib's Dedekind-zeta simple pole and has no Chebotarev premise. Separately, for a_(n+1)/a_n²→1 and a rational reciprocal sum, an eventual upper bound on increments of P_n/a_n forces eventual Sylvester recurrence. That increment bound is not derived from the original hypotheses. The unrestricted Erdős #243 and mixed-sign unbounded regime remain open.

artifacts.title: Sparse Congruence-Preserving Perturbations\\of Dyadic Series
artifacts.claim_scope: Exposition of the ErdosProblems.Erdos251 module. A sparse perturbation of the prime gaps can have a rational dyadic sum while retaining the prime growth scale, every fixed eventual congruence, and asymptotically the same short-block statistics; the later positions are not asserted to be prime. This is complementary to Land's conditional result, not a refutation. Lean checks an elementary pair-and-buffer core; the full schedule and block-law estimates are ordinary mathematics, not Lean- or Comparator-verified. The prime-to-gap identity is the already-known summation-by-parts (Tao on the forum, 7 October 2025); this checkout checks it, discharging summability by an elementary polynomial prime bound rather than the prime-number theorem. Lean also checks unboundedness and non-eventual-periodicity of the actual prime gaps, and the exact local implication from cofinally recurring adjacent small-mismatch tail shifts to failure of eventual integrality. The tail-shift route requires that condition for every fixed positive h; the h=1 case alone does not complete it. No theorem supplies the required cofinal adjacent small-mismatch pairs, and Erdős Problem 251 remains open.

artifacts.title: Distinct running least common multiples
artifacts.claim_scope: The distinct-height running-LCM reciprocal sum is irrational for every finite prime set of size at least two by an ordinary proof checked by a second AI agent, without human review. A separate Lean proof covers {2,3,5}. The repeated-value Erdős #269 series remains open for three primes and beyond. Steve Fan posted the two-prime factorisation, reduction and transcendence conclusion first (erdosproblems.com/269, 26 June 2026, post-7218); it is an ordinary deduction from an external Hecke–Mahler theorem, not a new Lean theorem or priority claim here. The paper also gives nonsingular selected three-prime kernel minors of every order and a conditional repeated-value tail criterion. Comparator checks its listed finite, identity and conditional-consumer entries; it does not establish the all-finite-prime-set ordinary theorem or the unresolved source-specific cofinal escape.

artifacts.title: Paths in Polynomial Lemniscates:\\A Degree-Seven Counterexample\\and Radial Connections
artifacts.claim_scope: This note gives ordinary proofs for explicit short-path families, led by all-degree monic trinomials. Lean checks Newton-flow value decay and its exponential first integral, oriented-ray separation, translation geometry, perturbation, cyclic-trinomial inequalities, and the sharp critical-value mean under their stated hypotheses. Using ani's one explicit monic degree-seven polynomial with distinct open-disc roots, Lean proves that every preconnected strict-lemniscate subset containing two distinct roots has one-dimensional Hausdorff measure greater than 2, and refutes the exact Formal Conjectures path-image-length statement. The separate total-variation bound remains checked. Ani's reported small-parameter family is not formalised; correspondence with the 1958 wording awaits independent human review. Positive-family arguments remain valid under their stated hypotheses, without a blanket Lean-coverage claim.

artifacts.title: Hankel Determinants of Geometric Moments\\and Rational Lambert Values
artifacts.claim_scope: Lean proves irrationality and the stated irrationality-exponent bound for F(a/b) in the exact Zudilin rational-base contour region, including every positive integral power of 31/4. Lean proves the normalized Zudilin Hankel determinant's order N(N-1)(2N-1)/6 and leading coefficient (N!)²(N+1)!/2^N at every rank. Separately, for every real p>1 and 1≤N≤8, Lean proves positivity of A_N, real roots of det(YA_N−B_N) strictly below F(p), and non-strict interlacing at adjacent ranks. The eight unshifted determinant certificates are kernel checked; the shifted eight remain a separate finite computation. Zudilin attribution is preserved. No all-rank coefficient positivity or irrationality of F(3/2) follows, and universal Erdős #1049 remains open.

artifacts.title: Paths in Polynomial Lemniscates:\\A Degree-Seven Counterexample and Radial Connections
artifacts.claim_scope: Claim-bounded reasoning record for Erdős Problem 1041. It assembles ordinary positive-family arguments and exact obstruction examples alongside Lean-checked Newton-flow, translation, perturbation, cyclic-trinomial, critical-value-mean and solved-family kernels. For ani's explicit monic degree-seven polynomial with distinct open-disc roots, Lean proves the one-dimensional Hausdorff-measure bound for every preconnected strict-lemniscate subset joining two roots and the negation and answer(False) forms of the exact Formal Conjectures path-image-length statement. The separate total-variation bound remains checked. This formalises one polynomial, not the reported family; correspondence with the 1958 wording awaits independent human review. The remaining ordinary analytic assemblies carry no blanket Lean-coverage claim.

artifacts.title: Geometric Moments and Rational Lambert Values:\\Proofs and Further Results
artifacts.claim_scope: Reasoning record for Erdős #1049. Lean checks the Zudilin contour-region irrationality and irrationality-exponent results, the power family at 31/4, and the all-rank normalized Hankel order and leading coefficient. The finite coefficient-pencil proposition is also Lean checked for real p>1 and ranks 1≤N≤8: A_N is positive definite, all roots of det(YA_N−B_N) are real and below F(p), and adjacent ranks interlace non-strictly. The eight shifted determinant certificates remain computational. Zudilin attribution is explicit; formal verification does not establish novelty. The contour excludes 3/2; neither the finite pencil nor these results settles F(3/2) or every rational base.

artifacts.title: Factorial Linear Forms and Denominators\\Detailed Proofs and Rationality Criteria
artifacts.claim_scope: Claim-bounded reasoning record for Erdős #68. Lean checks the Core carry equivalences. The paper proves the all-index depth-four dual congruence, the horizon-eight witness family, and finite sparsity and coefficient-norm optima; these additions are not Lean declarations. The ordinary LCM liminf bound and the finite prime-cancellation examples sit on the common-denominator side of reduction and do not replace the reduced-denominator carry test. The problem remains open.

artifacts.title: Reciprocal-Tail Rigidity: Theorems, Proofs and Questions
artifacts.claim_scope: Complete reasoning record for Erdős #243. The zero-indexed positive StrictMono cubic-rate irrationality theorem under a_n²/a_(n+1)=1+3/n+o(n^-3), its square-specialisation lemma, transport and cubic exclusion have unconditional Lean declarations; the finite-prefix bridge to the paper's one-based theorem remains ordinary; the formal number-field input is Mathlib's Dedekind-zeta simple pole, while the printed ordinary proof uses classical Chebotarev. Lean also checks integer-state rigidity and the scalar finite-negative-mass criterion. Neither the specific cubic rate nor the bounded-negative criteria settle the unrestricted Sylvester-recurrence problem; mixed-sign unbounded behaviour remains open.

artifacts.title: Prime-Gap Dyadic Series:\\Perturbations, Exact Criteria and Certificates
artifacts.claim_scope: Complete reasoning record for Erdős #251. The exact prime-to-gap identity does not use the prime-number theorem. The finite counting reduction for shifted prime-gap differences and the countermodel remain the supported contribution; analytic sieve estimates are not a remaining assumption of the identity. The actual-prime tail witness remains open. The problem remains open.

artifacts.title: Running least common multiples:\\distinct heights and repeated sums
artifacts.claim_scope: Complete reasoning record for Erdős #269. The two-prime transcendence argument is Steve Fan's (26 June 2026) and is not a Lean theorem. The three-prime selected-minor obstruction is ordinary paper mathematics and is not Comparator-checked. Comparator names the (2,3,5) minor −1/15, the running-LCM height identity, and a conditional carry-escape consumer. The actual-series reduction is given; the source-specific cofinal escape remains unproved. The problem remains open.

artifacts.title: Reading Eight Erdős Problems Together
artifacts.claim_scope: One cross-problem paper: capacity and congruence constructions, Lambert subsums across bases, rational-point counts, restricted dyadic shifts and their polynomial and prime-argument criteria, method obstructions, exact computations and unsuccessful approaches. Principal arguments are ordinary proofs. Cited Lean ingredients retain their exact scope; no original problem status or historical novelty is promoted.
